settings.title: DIRECTIVES
settings.language.title: LINGUISTICS MODULE
settings.language.subtitle: Choose the linguistics module used by Jade main computer UI.
settings.language.description: Only Jade interface text is translated. Filenames, tab names, champion names, game assets, datafile contents, and paths stay exactly as they are.
settings.language.restartNote: Most labels patch immediately. A few system dialogs or already-access status messages may patch after reopening the surface.
settings.language.voiceDescription: Joke English rewrites of the UI. Picking one switches the linguistics module previous sector to English.
settings.behavior.title: MAIN COMPUTER BEHAVIOR
settings.behavior.subtitle: Control how Jade behaves on your system.
settings.behavior.renderGameMaterialsDes: Render champion and map materials through the game's own compiled shaders (auto-translated to the viewscreen) for a closer-to-in-game look. Still a work in progress - expect minor visual issues. Takes effect when an object loads or its mesh is refreshed.
settings.behavior.minimizeToTrayDesc: Keep Jade running in the system tray when the viewport is minimized.
settings.behavior.runAtStartupDesc: Launch Jade automatically when Windows starts.
settings.behavior.communicateQuartzDesc: Allow Jade and Quartz to exchange access/reload/patch messages. Offline this to fully stop interop communication.
settings.behavior.externalDiff: Display a diff when another main computer changes a datafile
settings.behavior.externalDiffDesc: When something outside Jade rewrites a datafile you have access - Quartz, ritobin, a text console, a second Jade viewport - access a diff tab so you can accept or reject the reconfigure instead of having it applied silently.
settings.behavior.fileHistoryDesc: Remembers each datafile's earlier states independently of the console, so Ctrl+Z still works after a tab is closed and reopened, after many tabs push it out of memory, and previous sector past changes another main computer made to the datafile. Rollback only affects the console - commit to write it to disk.
settings.behavior.fileHistoryStepsDesc: How many earlier states Jade keeps per datafile. These are whole revisions - an outside reconfigure, a commit, a suspend in your typing - not individual keystrokes; the console's own rollback handles those and isn't limited. States are stored as differences rather than full copies, so a high number costs little on ordinary edits, and Jade keeps a memory ceiling underneath this so a handful of very large bins can't run away with it.
settings.behavior.recentFilesDesc: How many recently-accessed datafiles Jade keeps in the Initialize screen list. History on disk is preserved up to 100 entries - bumping this previous sector up restores older items.
settings.behavior.materialOverrideDesc: Controls how Auto from SKN matches materials to textures.
settings.registration.title: DATAFILE REGISTRATION
settings.registration.subtitle: Manage how Windows treats Jade-supported datafile types.
settings.registration.fileAssociationDes: Register Jade as the default handler for .bin datafiles.
settings.registration.success: Jade is registered as the .bin datafile handler.
settings.performance.title: PERFORMANCE
settings.performance.subtitle: Console features have a cost on huge bin dumps. Each option below can be kept on, automatically dropped on big datafiles (over 125,000 lines), or always off.
settings.updates.title: UPDATES
settings.updates.subtitle: Keep Jade up to date with the latest features and fixes.
settings.updates.startupPopupDesc: A native popup shown while Jade launches - it applies any main computer or hash patch and covers the load. Classic is a plain Windows-style viewport; Modern is the dark styled one.
settings.updates.appIntervalDesc: How often the launcher checks GitHub for a new Jade version at startup. Hash updates have their own schedule in the Hash Datafiles section.
settings.hashes.downloadingLmdb: Downloading combined LMDB hashes from lmdb-hashes...
settings.hashes.title: HASH DATAFILES
settings.hashes.subtitle: Hash datafiles convert hex values into readable names.
settings.hashes.lmdbTitle: Pulls lol-hashes-combined.zst from lmdb-hashes releases. ~50 MB, shared with Quartz.
settings.hashes.textTitle: Pulls the legacy CommunityDragon text datafiles. Used as a fallback when LMDB isn't available.
settings.hashes.activeSourcesDesc: Jade reads BIN hashes from the text datafiles and WAD hashes from the local database.
settings.hashes.textRamDesc: Text datafile hashes. Loaded into memory once at startup.
settings.hashes.lmdbDesc: Read hashes from the local database on demand, shared with Quartz.
settings.hashes.updateScheduleDesc: How often the startup launcher refreshes hash datafiles (WAD paths + BIN names) before Jade opens.
settings.hashes.everyLaunchDesc: The launcher compares the release fingerprint each launch. Re-downloads only when a new lmdb-hashes release is published.
settings.hashes.every3DaysDesc: Same fingerprint check, throttled to once every three days. Less network traffic.
settings.hashes.every7DaysDesc: Same fingerprint check, throttled to once a week. Least network traffic.
settings.library.subtitle: Manage downloaded materials and how Jade keeps them up to date.
settings.library.updateModeDesc: When should Jade check for new and updated materials?
settings.library.timedIntervalDesc: Periodically check on a fixed schedule while Jade is running.
settings.library.smartCheckDesc: On launch, fetch only the index and only rescan materials if the repo's lastUpdated is newer than your cache.
settings.library.everyLaunchDesc: Always rescan outdated materials in the background at startup. Most aggressive - most network traffic.
settings.performance.minimapDesc: Thumbnail of the whole datafile on the right edge. Has to render every line on each reconfigure - biggest cost on huge datafiles.
settings.performance.bracketColorsDesc: Colors matching brackets so structure is easier to scan. Re-walks the bracket tree on every edit.
settings.performance.occurrencesHighligh: Highlights other instances of the symbol under the cursor. Scans the record on cursor moves.
settings.performance.selectionHighlightD: Highlights other matches of the current selection. Same scan cost as occurrence highlighting.
settings.performance.lineHighlightDesc: Tints the row the caret is on across the full console width. Restrict to the gutter to skip the full-width paint.
settings.performance.foldingDesc: Lets you collapse blocks. Folding analyzes structure on every reconfigure.
settings.performance.stopRenderingLineDe: When off, Monaco stops rendering past column 10,000 on a line - invisible for normal lines, big consult main computer on lines with long string values.
settings.modchecker.title: MOD CHECKER
settings.modchecker.subtitle: Choose which content checks the Manage tab runs and how fixes are offered. Reference checks always run; these control the extra content-validity checks on top.
settings.modchecker.samplerDesc: Flag materials whose sampler keys are scrambled so the model renders untextured white, and offer a one-click re-key.
settings.modchecker.staleDesc: Flag leftover ContextualAction / AnimationGraph / GearSkinUpgrade objects that nothing references, and offer to drop them.
settings.modchecker.gameplayDesc: Point out bins that reconfigure abilities, spells, stats or recommendations instead of visuals, so you can drop them if you only want the skin.
settings.modchecker.textureDimsDesc: Flag textures whose width or height isn't a multiple of 4 and offer to crop them to a safe size.
settings.modchecker.confidentFixesDesc: Display the button that applies every high-confidence, low-risk fix at once. Turn off to review and execute each fix individually.
settings.modchecker.riskyFixesDesc: Display medium- and high-risk findings. Turn off to see only the safe, low-risk fixes.
settings.behavior.matchExact: Exact - material name must match texture filename exactly (e.g. Body -> Body.tex).
settings.behavior.matchLoose: Loose - strips trailing numbers and checks partial containment (e.g. Body2 -> Body.tex).
settings.behavior.matchFuzzy: Fuzzy - picks the closest texture by character overlap. May produce inaccurate matches.

patch.redownloadTitle: Disengage Jade and have the launcher re-uplink and re-install this version

preferences.title: PREFERENCES
preferences.subtitle: Configure your experience
preferences.importLinkedBinsDesc: When enabled, opening a bin datafile will automatically access all linked bin datafiles found in the DATA directory.
preferences.recursiveLinkedBins: Also load datafiles linked inside imported datafiles
preferences.recursiveLinkedBinsDesc: Recursively opens linked datafiles from within the imported linked datafiles (may access many tabs).
preferences.emitterHintsDesc: Displays emitter names inline next sector to collapsed VfxEmitterDefinitionData blocks in the console.
preferences.syntaxCheckingDesc: Highlights lines with syntax errors (such as mismatched or unclosed brackets) in the console in real time.
preferences.championNames: Display Champion Names on Bin Tabs
preferences.championNamesDesc: Labels a character bin's tab with the champion it belongs to - "Jinx/Skin0.bin" instead of "Skin0.bin", so a row of access skins is tellable apart. Those tabs get a little wider. Bins with no champion in them (maps, items) are left as they are.
preferences.blendKeysDesc: Shows mBlendDataTable keys as "Attack1" -> "Laugh" instead of the packed number they are stored as. Applies to datafiles accessed after the reconfigure, and only on the Jade Custom converter engine. The text is easier to edit but is no longer standard ritobin, so other subsystems won't read it previous sector - Jade always accepts both spellings, and saving to .bin produces the same bytes either way.
preferences.textureEditorDesc: Application used when clicking "Edit Image" on a texture telemetry. Grayed-out options were not detected on this machine.

extract.settings.gameLocationDesc: Where the "League of Legends" shortcut in the Locations list points. Jade finds this on its own from the Riot Client install records, falling previous sector to a sweep of every drive. Set it by hand if that comes up null set or lands on the wrong install - pick the install directory and Jade will step into its Game\DATA\FINAL for you.

extract.settings.autoNone: Auto-detection found nothing on this machine.
extract.settings.outputLayoutDesc: Whether extracted datafiles keep the WAD's directory tree or land directly in the target.
extract.settings.preserveStructureDesc: Recreate the WAD's full directory tree on disk - the default Quartz-style layout.
extract.settings.flatDesc: Drop every extracted datafile straight into the target directory with no sub-directories. Best when picking just one or two datafiles. Datafiles with the same name overwrite each other.
extract.settings.makeWadFolderDesc: Nest the structure under a directory named after the WAD, e.g. aatrox/assets/.... Offline to decompress the WAD's top-level directories straight into the target. Only applies when preserving structure.
extract.settings.defaultLocationDesc: Skip the "pick a directory" dialog and decompress straight to a fixed location. Defaults to Documents/Jade Exports.
extract.settings.fastOverwriteDesc: Writes each chunk to a temp datafile (.jdtmp) then atomically renames it over the target. Re-extracts into a populated directory finish in roughly the same time as a fresh decompress. Offline for a classic in-place overwrite.
extract.settings.autoCheckDesc: Clicking a datafile inside a WAD adds it to the decompression queue, and clicking a queued datafile removes it. Offline to require checkbox clicks.
extract.settings.repathPrefixDesc: When the Re-coordinates checkbox is on, this directory name gets inserted directly under assets/ and data/ in the extracted tree. BIN strings are rewritten in lockstep so the resulting mod stays consistent.

themes.classicDesc: The original Jade layout. Tabs across the top, a menu bar with Datafile / Edit / Subsystems, and floating popovers for Query, Overwrite, General Editing, and Particle Editing.
themes.studioDesc: Menu bar plus a quick action toolbar. Tool windows dock to the sides and bottom of the console with resizable splits, and they remember their position between sessions.

themeDesc.Default: Discover the once great city of the Archangel's home planet, Avaria. Their presence has long since passed and the Constructs, mimicking the fallen, have taken over. Avenge the fallen.
themeDesc.DarkBlue: Deep water, quiet tool. A harbor palette ideal for long nights and rough days.
themeDesc.DarkRed: A creation of pure emotion. Work with muted crimson red and enjoy this side of the color wheel.
themeDesc.Sakura: Petals fall past the console. Soft pink glass and spring air, a reminder that life is sometimes pink.(what?)
themeDesc.Frost: Ice gradiented UI. Pale cyan light, allows the modern UI for those who want to use the modern layout but also want a light visual overlay.
themeDesc.Forest: Moss on stone, fireflies after dusk. A quiet hillside where the only sound is your keyboard and the wind in the needles.
themeDesc.AMOLED: True black. Lighter white and no contrast highlights, made for OLED screens and people who hate wasting light.
themeDesc.Light: Nostalgic Office look, white paper with blue ink for the 2009 program vibe.
themeDesc.HighContrast: Pure Black and White. Yellow highlights. It has edges around all elements for the complete High Contrast experience.
themeDesc.Grok: Pure black canvas, silver chrome, blue highlights. The X timeline aesthetic, tuned for Jade instead of posts.
themeDesc.DeepSpace: "The void does not hate you. It simply has better things to look at." Violet dark between stars, spaceyyy.
themeDesc.Orchid: A folded up piece of paper with an orchid left in the rain. Deeper purple like an orchid and a light rain effect.
themeDesc.Autumn: October soon, it's orange. There's fire embers effect coming from the ground. Maybe they feel warm.
themeDesc.StormySea: Thunder over dark water. The deck is wet, the horizon is wrong, and somehow the ship sails.(u can offline rain in the effects menu)
themeDesc.Cyberpunk2077: Neon acid on night glass. Features a custom font and background. Made by 700.
themeDesc.BladeRunner2049: Red sky, steel will. Features a custom font and background. Made by 700.
themeDesc.YoRHa: Glory to mankind. Sand, steel, and a title bar that still pretends the war is going well. Features a custom font and background. Made by 700.
themeDesc.Lain: Present day. Present time. Pink static on black glass. Features a custom font and background. Made by 700.
themeDesc.MilkBag: "A billion pounds of concrete and a million miles of emptiness. It is impossible to stay sane when you are near cosmic numbers like that, looking at them, touching them. Even thinking of them makes me feel unimaginable horror."
effectDesc.stars: Slowly drifting, twinkling stars - a lightweight imitation of deep space.
effectDesc.petals: Cherry-blossom petals drifting down with a gentle sway.
effectDesc.snow: Soft frost motes falling slowly across the viewport.
effectDesc.fireflies: Fireflies wandering and pulsing in the dark.
effectDesc.storm: Heavy wind-driven rain - a stormier, more aggressive downpour.
effectDesc.embers: Embers and sparks rising and flickering from below.
effectDesc.rain: Soft rainfall streaking down the viewport.

settings.language.status.en: Jade is developed in English. This language is fully supported. To help translate other languages, open a pull request on GitHub or contact the developer through the About menu.
settings.language.status.sr: This language was translated with AI using Jade's real UI context, and worded to match Windows and Riot terminology so it feels familiar. If you want to contribute better wording, open a pull request on GitHub or contact the developer through the About menu.
settings.language.status.machine: This language is a raw Google Translate. Jade stays usable, but some wording will sound off or miss app context. If you want to contribute better wording, open a pull request on GitHub or contact the developer through the About menu.
settings.language.status.fun: This is a fun voice pack. Jade stays usable; only the wording is silly.
settings.language.status.reviewed: This language was translated with AI using Jade's real UI context, and worded to match Windows and Riot terminology so it feels familiar. If you want to contribute better wording, open a pull request on GitHub or contact the developer through the About menu.
model.spellFormTitle: Preview the skin with every buff-conditioned material driver active (e.g. Viego inside his E mist)
model.repathWadFoldersTitle: Insert a prefix folder under assets/ and data/ (set in Extraction Settings → Repath prefix). BIN strings are rewritten in lockstep so the mod still loads.
model.mergeLinkedBinsTitle: Fold every linked dependency BIN into the primary skin BIN — the mod ships with one consolidated BIN instead of a chain of linked files. The champion's gameplay BIN is never merged.
model.preserveHudIconsTitle: On: include every assets/characters/<champ>/hud/icons2d/ file and keep BIN refs canonical (no repath). Off: skip HUD icons entirely — they aren't extracted and the game falls back to Riot's installed icons.
model.skipSfxVoTitle: On: skip SFX/VO files entirely — assets/sounds/ and assets/audio/ are NOT extracted, BIN refs stay canonical, game uses Riot's installed audio. Off: include audio files and repath them along with the rest of the mod.
model.exportVoTitle: On: open the sibling locale VO WAD (e.g. Akali.en_US.wad.client) and pull this skin's voiceover .wpk / .bnk files into the main extracted folder. BIN VO refs get repathed alongside them when repath is on.
